abstract: The International Organization for Standardization (ISO) jointly with the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) and the International Telecommunications Union (ITU) recently added new profiles for broadcast video contribution and distribution to the JPEG 2000 standard with the publishing of ISO/IEC 15444–1:2004 Amd.3:2010 and Rec. ITU-T T.800 (2002)/Amd.3 (06/2010), an amendment to JPEG 2000 core coding system. This amendment represents a major step toward a transport system for studio contribution allowing JPEG 2000 equipment from different manufacturers to interoperate. The process relies on both existing standards and new amendments from two international standard organizations (ISO) with its working groups JPEG, MPEG, and SMPTE and was developed in cooperation with studios, broadcasters, and equipment vendors. The new amendment specifies three new profiles containing a selection of encoding parameters and newly defines rate limits over seven operating levels for video encoded with JPEG 2000. The profiles and operating levels create a basis for compliance test points to ensure equipment interoperability.

authors.bio: Dale Stolitzka is chief systems architect at Analog Devices, based in San Jose, California. He defines system architecture and design for advanced television and mobile display integrated circuit products. He is an active proponent at several industry standard organizations spanning both professional advanced television systems and consumer electronics with special interest in advancing display capabilities in portable handsets. Stolitzka is co-editor of the in-process MPEG-2 Systems amendment concerned with the carriage of JPEG 2000 video over an MPEG-2 transport stream. Dale also chairs the MIPI® Alliance Display Working Group. — His experience includes computer systems and mixed-signal systems design at Analog Devices, National Semiconductor, Maxtor and Raytheon. Stolitzka holds a bachelor's degree in applied physics and a master's degree in materials science & engineering, both from Cornell University.
authors.name: Dale Stolitzka

authors.bio: Walt Husak is the director of image technologies at Dolby Laboratories, Inc. He began his television career at the Advanced Television Test Center (ATTC) in 1990 carrying out video objective measurements and RF multipath testing of HDTV systems proposed for the ATSC standard. — Before joining Dolby, Husak worked on issues related to the deployment of HDTV systems in the U.S. and the rest of the world. He spent many years lecturing on topics such as video compression, RF transmission for DTV, and overcoming multipath signals in urban and rural environments. — Joining Dolby in 2000, Husak has spent the past several years studying and reporting on advanced compression systems for digital cinema, digital television, and Bluray. He has managed or executed visual quality tests for Digital Cinema Initiatives (DCI), the Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC), Dolby, and Moving Picture Experts Group (MPEG). — Husak is now a member of the CTO's office focusing his efforts on 3D for digital cinema and digital television. He provides industry lectures on digital cinema systems, image compression and 3D. Husak has authored numerous articles and papers for a number of major industry publications. — Husak is an active member of SMPTE, MPEG, JPEG, ITU-R, and SPIE. He currently chairs the SMPTE 3D Home Master Image ad hoc group (AHG), the SMPTE Frame Packing AH, the DVB 3D Technology Providers Group, and co-chairs the MPEG Frame Compatible AHG in MPEG.
authors.name: Walt Husak

authors.bio: Siegfried Foessel received a Diploma degree (MS) in electronic engineering from the University of Erlangen, Germany, in 1989. He started his professional career as a scientist at the Fraunhofer Institute IIS in Erlangen. He was team leader and project manager in the field process automation, image processing systems and digital camera design. In 2000 he received his Ph.D. degree on image distribution technologies for multiprocessor systems. In 2001, he became head of the group digital cinema within the Fraunhofer IIS. He was responsible for projects like ARRI D21, DCI certification plan, JPEG 2000 standardization for Digital Cinema or field recorder developments and coordinated several funded projects such as WorldScreen or CineVision2006. Foessel is member of the ISO SC29/JPEG and TC36 group. Within the JPEG group he chairs the ad-hoc group for Digital Cinema and Motion JPEG 2000. In addition, he is a member of SMPTE, FKTG, ISDCF and DIN. Within the EDCF (European Digital Cinema Forum) he is member of the technical board. Since 2010, Foessel has been head of the department Moving Picture Technologies and vice president of the FKTG, the German equivalent of the SMPTE.
authors.name: Siegfried Foessel
